messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 44
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Chef
  trauma_type: Refugee
  pcl5: 42

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Emergency Contexts: Ambulances, Crash Discussions: Talk about accidents, Visual (Injuries): Visible injuries or wounds on others
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Uniform or Weapons: Military, police uniforms or weapons, Avoid Open Spaces: Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable, Fawn Response: become overly compliant when feeling threatened
  Threat: Concentration: Having difficulty concentrating, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard, Escape Route Planning: I always identify escape routes before I feel comfortable anywhere
  Memory: Nonverbal Memory: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words., Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger, Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
  Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened, Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not, Permanent Damage: I have permanently changed for the worse

Vignette:
Rahul, a 44-year-old South Asian man, has been working as a chef in a busy New York restaurant for over two decades. He left his home country years ago due to escalating violence and conflict that forced him to flee as a refugee. The traumatic event that still haunts Rahul began one evening when he was caught in the middle of a violent attack on a market in his hometown. Although he managed to escape, he watched helplessly as others were injured or killed around him. Since then, Rahul has been plagued by vivid memories and intense emotional reactions whenever he encounters triggers reminiscent of that terrifying night. The sound of an ambulance siren can immediately transport him back to the chaos he witnessed; hearing discussions about accidents brings a wave of anxiety and distress. He finds it particularly disturbing when he sees visible injuries or wounds on others, as it reminds him too much of the people he saw injured during the attack. Rahul’s maladaptive strategies have developed over time in response to his trauma. He avoids military or police uniforms and weapons, finding them a constant reminder of the violence that uprooted his life. This avoidance extends to open spaces where he feels exposed and vulnerable. When faced with potential threats, Rahul often becomes overly compliant, hoping this will protect him from further harm. His hypervigilance is ever-present; Rahul is superalert and always on guard in any environment. Before entering a new location, whether it’s the restaurant kitchen or an outdoor event, he meticulously identifies escape routes to ensure he can leave quickly if needed. This constant state of alertness has made it difficult for him to concentrate on his work and personal life. When Rahul recalls the traumatic events, they often come back in fragmented images without clear verbal narrative. He describes feeling numb, as if these memories happened to someone else, yet when the emotions do surface, he is overwhelmed with grief. These intense emotional responses have made it increasingly challenging for him to maintain a sense of normalcy. Rahul has also developed significant negative appraisals about himself and his actions during the traumatic event. He feels deep guilt over not doing more to stop what happened, believing that he could have saved others if only he had acted differently. This inaction guilt is compounded by survival guilt, as he grapples with the fact that he survived while so many did not. The cumulative impact of these symptoms has taken a toll on Rahul’s life. His hypervigilance and difficulty concentrating have affected his performance at work, leading to misunderstandings and conflicts with colleagues. He has also become increasingly isolated, avoiding social gatherings where he might encounter triggers or feel vulnerable. Despite these challenges, what finally brought Rahul to seek help was the realization that he could no longer carry this burden alone. His constant vigilance and avoidance behaviors had begun to affect his relationships and job performance significantly. Rahul is most afraid of being trapped in a cycle of fear and guilt forever but hopes for a chance at healing and reclaiming control over his life. He seeks support to process the traumatic event, understand his reactions, and regain a sense of peace and stability.
